item.title: SCP Reference Help
item.description: I need help to determine if any SCPs exhibit these concepts I have. 6000+ SCPs is a lot to comb through.
item.content:encoded:
I've seen a number of SCPs myself, but not enough. So at the moment there are 2 ideas that might have some potential.

1) An object that can observe past histories

2) A D-class that does not die

.

With the first, I originally concepted this object being a magnifying glass, however I did note after conception that there's a magnifying glass entry on some knock-off SCP website that refers to themselves as scp classic? Store, cache, preserve? Even if it isn't canon I think my concept can be mixed up a bit more than taking that specific form.

The key element is that this object would be able to reference an edit log for anything that is seen through it. You know, how on some of these posts you can see an edit history? That's the idea, but it could be all contents ever written on a whiteboard. Or in a notebook. But even deeper, say in a long held manuscript; like the Quran, or the Bible. Maybe even ████████ material? Naturally the key to this concept would be in the story surrounding it, but I want to know if this idea exists in the scp lore in anyway. I'm sure people have used time travel in their creation, but this specific trait just might be limiting enough to push a tale.

I do comprehend, being able to see redacted material is a dangerous idea, being that author makes that information unavailable to guide the mystery of it. But if used correctly, it has good potential to revive an old topic. Obviously requires a test of scrutiny.

.

The second concept is a lesser one in which I simply considered: What if there was a D-class that always survived their testing? If we apply this nature to a soldier or a doctor? Sure, there is some possibility, but D-class always gets the worst of it. So again, I want to know if there's any D-class that are SCPs.

This idea has less wiggle room being, at the moment, it's just an entity with writers shield. But there might be some fun to be had with this concept. P.S. I am not thinking of a character trait like Marvel's Darwin, where his body just adapts to any situation. Not my intent what-so-ever. Nor do I wish to pursue some "he's just lucky" trait akin to Domino. What would the D-class be I dunno, but I don't want to start concepting if there's already another similar D-class on the list.

.

If you can help I'd dearly appreciate it.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlights] The Ambassador's Strolling Players
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation's researchers are invited to take in a terrible show and rewarded with intelligence at the cost of nightmares.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

A Foundation researcher discovers a letter on their desk, inviting them to join a fellow scholar in taking in a show. The letter comes with a ticket to see "The Ambassador's Strolling Players" and instructions to burn it on a certain time and date.

Under heavy monitoring, the researcher complies and is transported to what appears to be a renaissance era opera house. Once arrived he is greeted by a strange crow man who tells him to stay silent through the performance and meet him back by concessions during the intermission.

The crow man then sits the researcher down in a massive theater filled with other strange creatures. On stage a disturbing show is performed showing a group of masked individuals convincing a strange creature they have its best interests at heart before betraying it in the end.

An intermission is called and the crow man joins the researcher by the concession stand. He says he needs to say as little as possible, and nothing even resembling a name can be used here. He hands the doctor a packet filled with enhanced containment procedures for some of the Foundation's most nasty SCPs.

They watch the conclusion of the play, seeing the "heroes" in masks bringing forth all of the riches they stole from the strange creature before "The Ambassador" who accepts them with a nod, which the masked actors receive with almost orgasmic delight.

Then the crow creature offers the researcher "a lift back" and teleports the researcher back to the test site before leaving.

The containment strategies the crow creature provided prove to be extremely effective in preventing breaches.

Other researchers in the Foundation begin receiving similar messages, inviting them to see other grotesque plays in exchange for valuable intelligence.

This goes on for some time until at one point, a researcher arrives at the opera house to see the actor who played "The Ambassador" in the crow's place. It gives the researcher a box that turns out to contain the crow's head and the researcher arrives back at home.

No further tickets are received.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: "Most likely SCP-XXXX is neutralized, but if you receive a ticket, you are to await an O5 vote before taking further action. Someone out there took a big risk to help us and it cost him everything. We cannot allow it to cost us everything too."

Additional Notes: I look forward to your comments!

item.title: Ultimate Digital Assistant
item.description: The digital assistant that knows anything anomalous.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Unsure. It doesn't fit into anything else

Page Layout (Optional): Classic

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is an entity on a phone that knows things, even in the future, to excruciating detail. It also calls itself "Watson"

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is an entity that took the place of Siri on an iPhone that sounds like a British Male. The tip of the iceberg is that it knows anything about anything non-anomalous. For example, ask it about what someone else ate for lunch on a certain day, and SCP-XXXX will tell what that person ate, down to the brand of the ingredients and where they came from. It doesn't know anything about anomalous objects though. It will say "I don't have any information on that."

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The dark side of SCP-XXXX is that its voice will progressively become raspier and raspier and filled with coughs over time. Once exactly three months pass, one person with a voice matching a Man with a British Accent within a range of 70 meters disappears and SCP-XXXX's voice will become clear again. If no one who fits the bill is within range, a random person will vanish and SCP-XXXX will change to that person's voice. SCP-XXXX says that this happens because it needs to sustain itself and "Don't worry about the disappearances".

Additional Notes: I have a feeling this has been done before or something similar has popped up, I'll need to know. I'll elaborate more on its personality if need be or how testing logs would play out or progress.

item.title: SCP concept Investigator Poz
item.description: a Private investigator drawn towards SCPs
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Hook: A Private Investigator has been seen at multiple (31) instances near newly discovered SCPs. Seems to be unaffected by many SCPs and Amnestics.

Central Narrative: Investigator Poz has been very elusive to the foundation and could be used as an asset. He, also, seems to know of SCPs and how to find them. Recently he has been seen to be unaffected by SCP-XXXX (Death-bringer #324) an SCP that predicts deaths. He was also unaffected by SCP-XXXX (Nightshift Hellscape) a place that affects people beyond repair mentally or otherwise. Investigator Poz has not been located as of yet.

Page Layout: Containment procedures and SCP information first. Then the instances of where he has been sighted.

Elevator Pitch: The Private Investigator known as Investigator Howard Poz has been spotted at multiple sites of SCPs (31 known instances). He is drawn to SCPs for some anomalous reason not yet discovered. The reason the foundation knows this is an anomalous property is because he has found 3 in Russia, 2 in China, 4 in Canada, 12 across the USA, 3 in Brazil etc. Finding one or two is natural, but finding 31 before the foundation is unnatural. He seems to be unaffected by amnestics up to Class C if not more. All the SCPs he has been seen at are newly discovered. The foundation does not know if he is creating the SCPs or just discovering them. If the latter is true he could make a good asset for the foundation. However if the former is true, we need to take immediate action to secure the Investigator.

Level 3 Clearance required

The SCP known as Investigator Poz has been catalogued with 3 anomalous properties.
1. Immunity to Amnestics
2. Immunity to most SCP affects
3. The ability to create beings or objects with anomalous properties

Level 4 Clearance required

Based on interviews from the populace who have met the Investigator, he has stated that he is "cataloging" and "trying to prevent the utter destruction of the world."

Additional Notes: SCPs he has been spotted at will be recorded

item.title: (Seking Greenlight) World of the Wars
item.description: What's a peace?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: In various small enclaves around the world, the belligerents of all the world's wars have small military contingents that never surrendered. In truth, these enclaves are actually entrances to an alternate universe that serves solely to keep wars going, and created these enclaves for that purpose. Here, not only do no real-world wars ever end, the various factions have their own political intrigues including new wars, espionage, and support for others.

Central Narrative: Begins with the Foundation's arrival in the holdout of the Obskurakorps, which they think is a more mundane holdout, or at least as mundane as the Obskurakorps can be. Talks end up going hot after the Obskurakorps takes them to be one of their predecessor organisations trying to infiltrate them, resulting in the death of the Obskurakorps' and Wehrmacht's Fuhrer and a war between them as to who will be his successor, and the unfolding use of this as a proxy war by various factions to try to get the side that would be most beneficial to them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Seeing how societies change with anachronistic influences and eternal war, as well as how the balance of these wars shift and change in response to major events.

Additional Notes: This was largely inspired by post-WWII Japanese Holdouts, although the process of brainstorming it moved it far beyond being all that recognisable. I'm also not sure about having the Nazis be the ones who go into the Civil War, since I'm afraid that might be a bit overdone in alternate history scenarios where they win/don't get completely usurped.

After the foundation finds out and runs a series of tests with this designation, they designate the scp designation itself as scp-XXXX.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Jumping on the meta bandwagon- since the designation itself is an scp the designation itself has developed a conscious creating a paradox.

item.title: Youtube Channels Inspiration List (Work In Progress)
item.description: List of channels that can provide inspiration for SCP stories and writing in general.
item.content:encoded:
There are a great number of Youtube channels that produce content that can be really useful and inspirational when you work on SCPs and tales. I've collected quite a few myself over the years, so I thought it would be useful to make a list of Youtube channels that can help us write.

What I really want is contributions. I'm going to start the list, but I want to expand it as much as possible. I'm going to use a format that will make it as fast as possible for people to find what they're looking for. If you contribute, please use the following format:

1. Include a link to the channel (preferably the channel main page, not just a video from the channel).
2. The name of the channel.
3. The category that they channel fits in (see categories below, might add more as time goes).
4. Description of the content on the channel. Try to include a little bit about who might be interested in the channel. See below for a framework.

Also note: The channel has to be somewhat directly relevant to writing SCPs. SCPs focus on phenomena that deviate from the norm. The list shouldn't include channels that delve into more mundane topics, even if those topics might be relevant to a story. It might be useful to research how a diesel engine works if you're writing a SCP focused on that topic, but it's not going to be even remotely useful to most people who write SCPs.

+ show block
– hide block

Youtube Channels

General Writing / Storytelling

Just Write
Link
Just Write focuses on looking at popular works of fiction, primarily movies, and trying to decipher what good lessons can be learnt from the work to improve your own writing.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to use popular works of fiction as a foundation to improve their own writing.

Lessons from the Screenplay
Link
Lessons from the Screenplay, obviously, focuses on screenplays, often focusing each video on a single movie, going over the screenplay to explain what makes it so effective. Has a lot of videos that focus greatly on dialogue.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to cinema for tips on how to build tension and write beautiful dialogue.

SCP specific content

The Exploring Series
Link
To many on these forums, The Exploring Series was the gateway drug to the rest of the SCP community. Each video goes over a single SCP, telling the tale of the SCP in an interesting and captivating way, combining the story with images appropriate to it.
Who is this for? Everyone, but especially people who are yet not that familiar with the SCP foundation.

Real life - Investigation and policework

JCS - Criminal Psychology
Link
JSC focuses on the psychology of criminals, using interrogation videos as his primary source of information.
Who is this for? This channel is an invaluable asset if you want to create realistic interrogation scenes in your writing.

Real Life - Psychology

Dr. Todd Grande
Link
Dr. Todd Grande focuses on making psychological profiles of real-life murders and serial killers. Some of his profiles focus on other interesting people who are somehow outliers of society.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to create much more realistic and grounded characters, especially evil or malevolent characters.

Real Life - Philosophy

Academy of Ideas
Link
A channel that goes into great detail on some of the darker writers in philosophy and psychology. The channel explores archetypes, shadow projection, despair and similar topics.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to learn more about the darker philosophers like Carl Jung, Nietzsche and Kirkegaard.

Real Life - Mysteries and peculiar phenomena

Lemmino
Link
Channel that focuses primarily on real life mysteries, like the Bermuda Triangle or Dyatlov Pass Incident.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to find information on the real life mysteries that often inspired SCPs.

Fiction - Horror

Acolytes of Horror
Link
Acolytes of Horror specializes in making fewer, but fairly long and in-depth analyses of horror. Primarily he analyses movies, but some of his videos focus on the historic influences on modern-day horror.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to really delve deep into the psychology and symbolism of effective horror.

The Vile Eye
Link
The Vile Eye makes psychological profiles of famous evil characters, from Nurse Ratchet in One Flew Over The Cuckoo's Nest, to Michael Meyers from Halloween.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to create a memorable evil character.

Ryan Hollinger
Link
Ryan Hollinger makes videos where he analyzes various horror movies, discussing what makes them effective.
Who is this for? Anyone looking to widen their background knowledge on horror movies.

Fiction - Thriller and Drama

Fiction - Science Fiction

Isaac Arthur
Link
This channel focuses on hard sci-fi topics such as Dyson Spheres and Matrioshka Brains as well as hypothesizes about aliens. A lot of the material might be a bit too large in scale to fit into the SCP universe.
Who is this for? Anyone who's interested in hard sci-fi and civilizations on a galactic scale.

John Michael Godier
Link
The creator of this channel is a science-fiction writer who focuses on hard sci-fi, with an emphasis on realism. The content describes a lot of hypothetical science fiction phenomena.
Who is this for? Anyone who's interested in hard sci-fi, especially concepts such as multiple universes and alien civilizations.

Like Stories of Old
Link
This channel is very philosophical, it goes into deep detail on topics such as time travel, the hero's journey, global pandemics and empathy. It can help create an emotional and philosophical underpinning to any story you tell.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to learn more about how sci-fi concepts and story tropes connect to a deeper philosophical and psychological truth.

Quinn's Ideas
Link
Quinn's Ideas focuses very heavily on the Dune universe, and as such goes into tremendous detail on topics such as psychic powers, genetics and omniscience. If you haven't read the Dune books, there are videos several hours long that go through each book. Has lately also started making videos on H.P. Lovecraft.
Who is this for? Anyone who wants to learn more about the Dune universe without reading all of the books. Also a great source of inspiration if you're writing on omniscience and related psychic powers.

Audiobooks

HorrorBabble
Link
Has all of the H.P. Lovecraft books, as well as many other horror writers such as Robert Bloch

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Eternal Pharaoh
item.description: Another Euclid humanoid SCP. Dated to be from ancient Egypt with potential knowledge of other anomalies.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Potential window into anomalous instances within Asia minor and Northern Africa.

Central Narrative: SCP that is believed to be a humanoid anomaly in the form of a mummy. While having two other sub anomalies if you would; The first being it's sarcophagus which is theorized to give the SCP a regenerative property, and the second sub anomaly being a collection of gold coins and a pair of curved swords found within the sarcophagus. Should these contents be taken more than 3.4M from the sarcophagus the SCP goes into a rage like state killing the thief and those whom attempt to stop it. Is also noted to be an anomaly that has the ORIA's attention, believed to be the result from a tip off from a worker at the excavation site the SCP was discovered at or by echelons by local governments just as the foundation was notified. Should also be noted that this SCP is not a fairly active one as unless disturbed will spend 72 hours in a hibernation state and up to one 24 hour period active.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP is believed to know more on other anomalies that were native to it's region through talks of missing "aljawayiz" / "الجوائز" or trophies in English. The anomaly is found to be rather cooperative and expresses willing to communicate with foundation personnel, but shares little of it's own past or own knowledge. Instead opting to learn more of the current world. The reasoning for this is unknown as the SCP seems to either hold only fragmented memories, or for unknown reasons is unwilling to share it's knowledge.

Additional Notes: I do have a presentable sandbox draft to share should someone like to see it. Sandbox potentially presents a better presented thought that is failed to be properly conveyed here due to user error.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch:

  • The core idea of this SCP is a child with C-PTSD from an unstable/abusive home life has developed anomalous properties, seemingly as a self-defense mechanism.
  • The child unknowingly manifests horrors that protect her in her sleep, but only in the event she has a nightmare.
  • The manifestation of these monsters will attack any other lifeform that comes within 3 meters of her as she slumbers.
  • The moment the child awakens from her nightmare, the monsters vanish, and the child is left with no inclination of what she has done - only that she's had a bad dream.

Central Narrative:
The child has been taken into Foundation care in an attempt to not only learn about her anomalies and why they seemingly manifested, and try to pinpoint what made these anomalies manifest in the first place.

Through trial and error the researchers assigned to her case begin to understand her condition, learn how to avoid potential manifestations of her monstrous protectors, and attempt to rehabilitate her in the process.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
The SCP within this story is just a normal little girl, who doesn't understand what is happening to her or why. She has no idea of her anomaly, only that she was "taken away" from her parents. This part I'm mildly struggling with. I feel like I have a good start here, I'm just not sure how to make this SCP stand out against thousands of others.

Additional Notes:
I have a good idea of what this SCP is, and what she can do, but I need a bit of help figuring out the specifics of her story. This is my first attempt at writing an SCP, and I want to make sure it's air tight before I even consider sending in a draft for serious critique. SCP-XXXX is a small patterned child's bed that emits a comforting attraction-aura of childhood and nostalgia. The bed makes any entity that sleeps in it have nightmares of green-glowing zombies attempting to eat their stomach. In dreams, people "get out of bed" in their current/old household (sometimes-combined).

After sleeping in the SCP, the user will have these nightmares every-time they go to sleep anywhere.
When having nightmares, people suddenly wake up in a panicked-state, which causes sleep deprivation. Some experience PTSD.

If multiple people feel the attraction of the SCP, all shall get aggressive at one-another and fight until one remains/all die. Aura-attraction to SCP is instant ONLY in a 10-feet radius to the SCP, and ONLY goes away for 9-to-15-minutes after awakening from it.

+ READ MORE
- READ LESS

Central-Narrative:

SCP-XXXX was found by Field-Agent, Chris, in Florida when investigating multiple reports of "eeriness" of an abandoned hospital from locals. Agent-C, under SCPs attraction-affect, realized the affect and called for backup. Three other Field-Agents arrived (with recording hardware) and found Agent-C sleeping in the SCP. All agents felt the affect of SCP, ending with a fight between the four agents where Agent-K killed all three other agents with a pistol and slept in the SCP.

Mobile Task Force Psi-7 was called in by Agent-K after waking up and leaving, which all twenty MTF were not able to contain the SCP due its attraction force. MTF member, Cadet-F, survived bloodshed and reported the incident after sleeping.

Agent-K and Cadet-F were taken into investigation with recorded evidence/interviews of what occurred.
Both were carefully watched over in-study by research staff, where Foundation realized consistent nightmares.
Both were given amnesics and therapy all which only helped endurance with the-nightmares and trauma. (SCP-500-use blocked by 05-council for scarcity-issues)

Agent-K was also questioned in later dates/interviews to describe any further issues he experienced (such as nightmares).

The SCP is left in the abandoned-building, guarded by 10 undercover guards looking like U.S-police to ensure locals don't enter.
Only researchers/needed-personnel are allowed inside.

D-Class studies/interviews/experiments and small-animal research confirmed SCP's affects like nightmares, aura-attraction, PTSD, and sleep deprivation.

Based on real nightmares I had as a kid after playing the game "Nicktoons Unite!".

Unlike other Bed-SCPs, it anomaly/nightmares "sticks" to its users.

Story is short-&-sweet.

SCP-XXXX is a hydraulic press which from a first glance doesn’t seem that weird. It seems like just the ordinary hydraulic press located in different factories across the world. A part of the SCP file is dedicated to the retrieval of SCP-XXXX. One of the researchers of SCP-XXXX interviews Agent Ford who helped to retrieve the SCP. During this interview we learn about the circumstances in which SCP-XXXX has been found and contained.

After some searching the officers and a foundation agent named Ford found a pile of dead bodies, their tattooed flesh ripped from their bodies. And next to it SCP-XXXX (the tattooed hydraulic press).

After the retrieval of SCP-XXXX the reader gets to read about research performed on SCP-XXXX. The reader learns about the nature of SCP-XXXX’s anomylous abilities. For example: SCP-XXXX has two modes of existence. It has its hydraulic press body which have several tattooed flesh patches on its frame, and it also has a secondary body, which is a cat like being into which the tattooed press transforms.

Central Narrative: People frequently wondered why Dr. Jenna Lopez never seemed to mind that Dr. Briggs kept staring at her chest. Strangely, if anyone mentioned his ogling, both doctors would deny that he was ever looking, both appearing confused by the suggestion that such an event had ever occurred, until the events of August 9th, 2020. That day, at lunch in the cafeteria, Dr. Briggs was "enjoying the view", when suddenly, he started screaming.

+ show block
– hide block

Co-workers turned to him, only to find that his irises had turned a viciously-bright shade of magenta. He, in a panicked frenzy, claimed that this was the first time he had ever looked at her chest, then vehemently insisted that he'd seen the word "M I N E" appear on her as if carved into the exposed skin. Other researchers, including Dr. Lopez herself, glanced down, only to see nothing of the sort. Briggs tried to insist again, continuing to look at her as the security team was called, only for him to start screaming again, this time out of intense pain rather than shock. Briggs then went fully blind. Lopez was temporarily confined, and tests started being performed.

Note: Lopez seems to completely lack control or intention regarding these effects, such that SCP-XXXX is identified as solely her chest, rather than the woman herself.

Containment: Since only exposed skin seems to cause the effects described, Lopez is allowed to roam free so long as she continues to wear clothing that covers her bosom (as well as an SCP-commissioned undergarment to prevent the effects from seeping through non-opaque fabrics). The classification is, for the time being, safe.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: First, the humor and righteousness of an SCP that punishes perverts who stare at this poor woman's chest. Second, the idea and potential ethical debate of an SCP attached to a non-SCP human person.

It's containment is also a bit different since it can't be held in a containment cell this SCP is supervised and secured by 4 to 5 security personnel so the gas station doesn't move and the mirror doesn't affect personnel.

As he was washing his face, the Researcher began looking intently at the mirror and started scratching his arm uncontrollably, grabbed his hair and breathed heavily, showing signs of paranoia, then suddenly began acting against his own will and followed his reflection's movement. After a bit, the reflection smiled and grabbed a hammer, so did the Researcher, they both swung the hammer towards the mirror, shattering it, and the Staff member dropped dead in the bathroom with multiple cuts around his body. The Foundation later found the body and started studying the SCP, theorizing it's origin and it's containment.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The gas station is often moved between places and awaits for it's next victim, and what's interesting to note is that the individual starts becoming their own reflection and begins following it's movement. It swaps the real person with the reflection, sending the individual temporarily to another dimension, but even swapped the reflection (now taking the role as the real person) can't escape the mirror and will go back into it once the mirror's broken.

The area around the anomaly isn't alien in nature, as it is very similar to our own universe.
The body, however, seems to send signals that are telepathic in nature. However, the only thing the foundation was able to decipher said, "Please help."

Central Narrative: After a site was built around the SCP, explorations by MTF agents were made into the factory

Show
Hide

In the first exploration log, they find the woman and discover it's not the factory that has been the anomalous one (although it does have some slight anomalous properties itself), it was her. They then find a pinboard with a paper reading "Bring your kid to work day!" with a date on it, (we saw how that went). An unlocked laptop with an OS similar to windows. The owner of the laptop is named Janis Phenix, who is the anomaly. A document is open on the laptop, its Janis' journal, and she writes about how she was embarrassed to be one of the small group that actually participated in "bring your kid to work day" but says it doesn't matter because her boss told her to come to something called "The Creator Room," and it's making her anxious all day for some reason. The foundation unable to access the previous days of the journal, but was able to download it for some reason.
In the second exploration log, an MTF was sent to recover as much information as they could. They found documents on every employee, and they find out that Janis was an anomalous artist and crafter (NOT part of AWCY?) who made the teddy bear her son was holding. Another thing they find is a map of the factory, and find that the underground parts are bigger than the above ground.
Back at control, the files from the laptop are sent. In the previous pages of the journal, Janis was promoted to work on something called "Project Dramaturgy," commissioned by a group called The SCP agency (this should be a major clue, if not tell me), they didn't know what exactly what they were creating or what it would be used for, but they could care less as they had a budget bigger than anything they would ever get. They were told to make an anomalous human out of the materials they had given them, they worked on it for a while and were near finished. The journal ends with the journal entry of her being embarrassed about being one of the small group that actually brought their kids.
In the third exploration log, the team is sent to the lower floors, where they find "anomaly creators." In the room Janis' boss asked her to be in, the creator room, they find a large containment cell (that was most likely breached) and a sheaf of papers describing the experiment. Long story short the SCP commissioned the factory, and they experiment on SCP agency (the SCP foundation of their universe) D-class and attempted to make a human superweapon, everything was fine until Janis' son brought his anomalous teddy bear and it triggered a chain reaction that caused the breach (as stated before in the journal, she made the teddy bear while she wasn't experienced much with anomalies herself). The SCP foundation theorizes that every employee in the factory also experienced what Janis did and was moved to a separate universe.

+ Latest version (22/11/2020)

Central Narrative:

SCP-XXXX is a ordinary looking glass jar that can be closed with a metallic lid.

Eating solid food within a 20 meter radius around SCP-XXXX will make the subject bite on a tooth, appearing inside the food. This tooth, called SCP-XXXX-1, matches the DNA of the subject that bit on it, although no loss of tooth is observed on the subject.

This phenomenon can be repeated. Every time an instance of SCP-XXXX-1 is created, its mass is substracted from the subject's bone mass. Excessive repetition of the phenomenon may lead to bone diseases.

Placing instances of SCP-XXXX-1 into SCP-XXXX, closing it with the lid, and breaking all visual contact with it allow for the transmutation event to take place instantly. The transmutation replaces all instances of SCP-XXXX-1 with coins, referred to as SCP-XXXX-2.

Instances of SCP-XXXX-2 look identical to coins of the French Franc currency, melted in 1982. The SCP-XXXX-2 are highly radioactive, warranting their rapid disposal.

The article would describe the SCP in the usual objective fashion, complemented with tests to understand its properties :

For example, a log could feature uncomfortable D-classes eating through all sorts of food to test out which trigger teeth apparitions, and subsequently get diagnosed with some bone disease. Then, the article would show studies made about the transmutation, trying to understand exactly what kind of objects gets transmuted (do regular teeth also work?)

This would be a short article about a fun weird object that is at the same time somewhat cute (turning your fallen teeth into a small payment) and somewhat unsettling (teeth in your food, osteoporosis and radiations)


Hook/Attention-Grabber: Have you ever bitten on your own dislodged tooth while eating, when you were a child? It's not the most pleasant of sensations. This SCP also twists the tale of the tooth fairy in a SCP-esque fashion.
+ Version 1 (21/11/2020)
- Show less

Central Narrative:

SCP-XXXX is a ordinary looking glass jar that can be opened or closed with a metallic lid. Manufacturing codes engraved at the bottom of SCP-XXXX suggest it originally was a jar of Dijon mustard.

Eating solid food within a 20 meter radius around SCP-XXXX will have the following effect occur: after chewing four to five times, the subject will bite on a small human tooth, that was not initially present in the food. This tooth, called SCP-XXXX-1, matches the DNA of the subject that bit on it, although no loss of tooth is observed on the subject.

This phenomenon can be repeated. An instance of SPC-XXXX-1 will appear in the consumed food every four to five mastications, and this will always result in the subject biting onto it, leading to possible mouth injuries if unprepared.
Every time an instance of SCP-XXXX-1 is created, its mass is substracted from the subject's bone mass. Excessive repetition of the phenomenon on the same subject will result in the onset of bone-related diseases, such as osteoporosis.

Placing instances of SCP-XXXX-1 into SCP-XXXX, closing it with the lid, and breaking all visual contact with it allow for the transmutation event to take place instantly.
The transmutation event can occur only if no human person or camera has a visual contact with SCP-XXXX. The transmutation effectively replaces all instances of SCP-XXXX-1 with coins, referred to as SCP-XXXX-2.

Instances of SCP-XXXX-2 look identical to coins of the French Franc currency. Composition and engravings on the surface matches that of regular coins melted in 1982.
All instances of SCP-XXXX-2 are highly radioactive, averaging 80 μSv/h, warranting their rapid disposal.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: Have you ever bitten on your own dislodged tooth while eating, when you were a child? It's not the most pleasant of sensations. This SCP also twists the tale of the tooth fairy in a SCP-esque fashion.
